title: Worked examples for this(...) and base(...)
summary: Constructors now shows both kinds of constructor call in action.
items: A bank-account example of this(...) chaining and a vehicle-and-truck example of base(...), each with its output, both compiled and run before publishing.
What happens when base(...) is left out (compile error CS7036), four rules to remember, and a new quiz question.

title: The story behind C# and .NET, in the first lesson
summary: What Are C# and .NET? now explains why the platform was built the way it was.
items: How compiled C and C++ programs are tied to one operating system and processor, how Java solved that with bytecode and the Java Virtual Machine, and how Microsoft built C# and .NET on the same idea.
A new quiz question on platform dependency.

title: Updated for .NET 11 and C# 15
summary: .NET 11 and C# 15 were released on 10 November 2026. The course was updated the next day.
items: New Part XIII, What's New in .NET 11 and C# 15: ten beginner-friendly lessons on union types, closed hierarchies, collection expression arguments, extension indexers, labeled break and continue, runtime async, the new library APIs, ASP.NET Core 11 and EF Core 11.
A step-by-step checklist for upgrading a real project to .NET 11.
The setup and first-program lessons now install .NET 11 and target net11.0, with a note on .NET 10 as the long-term support release.
The cheat sheet, glossary and interview guide gained C# 15 syntax, terms and questions, and the file-based apps lesson covers what .NET 11 adds.

title: A .NET developer roadmap and faster pages
summary: A new planning guide, and a pass over speed and accessibility across the whole site.
items: New: the .NET developer roadmap, a stage-by-stage plan from your first program to production, with every stage linked to its lessons.
Pages load noticeably faster, and contrast, keyboard navigation and screen-reader support were improved everywhere.
Every lesson now shows the date it was last updated, and an RSS feed lists new and updated lessons.

title: Quizzes, progress and reading time
summary: Tools that help you learn, not just read.
items: Interactive quizzes: choose an answer and see straight away why it is right or wrong.
Reading time on every lesson, progress for each part, and a daily learning streak.
Code examples repaired in 163 lessons, and the mobile layout tidied.

title: A new design and four guide pages
summary: The course player was redesigned and the site gained its first guide pages.
items: Larger, easier-to-read type and a calmer palette in the course player.
New guides: Start Here, Interview Prep, the C# cheat sheet and the .NET glossary.
Every lesson page gained the full site navigation, so any lesson can be opened, bookmarked and shared on its own.

title: Reader mode and Listen to this lesson
summary: More comfortable ways to work through long lessons.
items: Adjustable text size, a distraction-free focus mode and a reading progress bar.
Listen to this lesson: your browser reads the lesson aloud.

title: The course is complete
summary: The Production .NET tier was finished, completing all three tiers, and the course moved to dotnetmadeeasy.com.
items: Production .NET: thirteen parts, from runtime internals and async to distributed systems, cloud, testing, modern C# 14 and the OrderFlow capstone.
Full-text search across every lesson, related-lesson suggestions and a “Was this lesson helpful?” control on each lesson.

title: C# In Practice tier complete
summary: The middle tier, for developers who know the basics, was published in full.
items: All 90 C# In Practice lessons: generics, LINQ, delegates and events, async, dependency injection, HTTP and data access, ending with complete projects.
C# Foundations Parts IV to VII: collections through practical development.

title: The course begins
summary: The first C# Foundations lessons were published, starting from what C# and .NET are and how to set up your machine.
